metric.why: A hall can be full by power and half empty by space, or the reverse. Tracking both per cabinet is how operators find capacity they already own before building more.
metric.metric: Stranded power and space per cabinet
metric.definition: Utility power or floor space that is allocated and paid for but cannot be used, because the other of the pair ran out first or airflow limits were reached.

reading.body:
Stranded power and space per cabinet is the metric that reveals hidden capacity inside existing data centers, making it possible to add compute without building new facilities.

Power and floor space inside a cabinet are consumed at different rates depending on the density and type of hardware installed. When power runs out before floor space is filled, the remaining rack units are unusable. When floor space is exhausted before the power allocation is spent, that power sits idle and paid for. Airflow constraints can strand both simultaneously, independent of either limit being reached on paper.

For AI workloads this matters directly. GPU-dense servers draw far more power per unit of floor space than general-purpose servers, which means a hall sized for conventional compute can exhaust its power budget while cabinets still appear half-empty by rack space. Operators who track stranded power and space per cabinet can find and correct that imbalance before requesting new utility capacity or breaking ground on additional space.

The data covers only the definition and operating rationale of this single metric. It does not provide actual stranding rates, facility counts, or comparisons across hardware generations, so no conclusion about how widespread the problem is can be drawn from it.
